test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 13 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements regarding the Himalayas is incorrect?

options.text: Kumaon is situated between the Himalayas, Sutlej and Kali rivers.
The outermost mountain range of the Himalayas is called Shivalik.
The Patkai Hills are situated between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik Range.
The Brahmaputra is located in the easternmost range of the Himalayas.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Patkai Hills are situated between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik Range.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Patkai Hills are not situated between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik Range.**
 
• The Patkai Hills are actually located in the northeastern part of India, forming the boundary between India and Myanmar.
 
• The Patkai Hills are part of the Purvanchal Range, which lies to the south of the Brahmaputra valley.
 
• The Purvanchal Range includes other hill ranges like the Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, Mizo Hills, and the Tripura Hills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Himalayas**

 
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in South Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• They are home to the planet's highest peaks, including the highest, Mount Everest in Nepal.
 
• The Himalayas include over fifty mountains exceeding 7,200 meters (23,600 ft) in elevation, including ten of the fourteen 8,000-meter peaks.
 
• The Himalayas have profoundly shaped the cultures of South Asia; many Himalayan peaks are sacred in Hinduism and Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Shivalik Range**
 
 
• The Shivalik Hills, also known as the Outer Himalayas, extend from the Indus River in the west to the Brahmaputra River in the east.
 
• They are the southernmost and geologically youngest east-west mountain chain of the Himalayas.
 
• The range is about 2,400 km long and varies in width from 10 to 50 km.
 
• The average height of the Shivalik Hills is between 900 to 1,200 meters (3,000 to 4,000 ft).
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra River**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra is one of the major rivers of the world, flowing in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, India, and Bangladesh.
 
• It is about 2,900 km (1,800 mi) long, and its drainage basin is 712,035 km² (274,918 mi²) in size.
 
• In India, it flows through the states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam before entering Bangladesh.
 
• The Brahmaputra plays a key role in the culture, economy, and ecology of the region through which it flows.
 
 
 
• **Kumaon**
 
 
• Kumaon is one of the two regions and administrative divisions of Uttarakhand, a mountainous state of northern India, the other being Garhwal.
 
• The Kumaon region is bounded on the north by Tibet, on the east by Nepal, on the south by the state of Uttar Pradesh, and on the west by the Garhwal region.
 
• It comprises the districts of Almora, Bageshwar, Champawat, Nainital, Pithoragarh, and Udham Singh Nagar.
 
• Kumaon is known for its scenic beauty, rich cultural heritage, and diverse flora and fauna.
